focus_area: Test correctness (ghost/tautological hunt across all 11 new/modified spec files) + adversarial second opinion on app/jobs/extract_job_criteria_job.rb and app/models/ai_job_criteria.rb (+ job.rb broadcast/guard methods)

findings.title: broadcast_completion dereferences ai_job_criteria.job.title with no nil guard on the job association
findings.description: In broadcast_completion, `jobTitle: ai_job_criteria.job.title` (line 54) dereferences the belongs_to :job association after re-reading the row (line 46). If the parent Job were deleted between extraction start and the broadcast, `.job` would be nil and this would raise NoMethodError inside the retry_on exhaustion block (which is NOT wrapped in a rescue), or inside the StandardError rescue. This is negligible in practice: `belongs_to :job` is required, jobs are not deleted mid-extraction, and the analog (generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb) uses the identical unguarded `.job_application...`/`.job.title` access pattern. A nil `title` (possible on a draft job) is not a crash — it only yields an empty toast interpolation, which is cosmetic. Traced: extract_job_criteria_job.rb:46-54 -> ai_job_criteria.rb belongs_to :job -> Job#title. Reported for completeness only; matches the adjudicated analog structure (item 10) and is not actionable.
findings.recommendation: No change required (matches analog). If defensiveness is ever desired, guard `jobTitle: ai_job_criteria.job&.title`.
